title: Pipeline API: optional constraint bounds must be checked with `is not None`, not truthiness (zero bounds were dropped)
answers: pipeline constrain Interval accepts negative numbers
zero bound ignored in pydantic experimental pipeline
body:
Symptom: with the experimental pipeline API, `validate_as(int).constrain(Interval(ge=0, le=10))` accepts -5, and `Interval(gt=0)` / `le=0` / `lt=0` let through 0 or values on the wrong side. Any bound of exactly zero (0, 0.0, Decimal('0')) was silently skipped.
Root cause: pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py:_apply_constraint unpacked `annotated_types.Interval` into Ge/Gt/Le/Lt using `if constraint.ge:` etc., so falsy-but-set bounds were treated as absent.
Fix pattern: test optional constraint fields with `is not None` before delegating to the per-bound constraint (`_apply_constraint(s, annotated_types.Ge(constraint.ge))`).
Constraints: applies to any optional numeric/length field on annotated_types constraints (bounds, min/max lengths, multiple_of) where 0 is a valid value; truthiness checks are only safe for fields where falsy really means 'unset'. Regression cases go in the `test_interval_constraints` parametrization in tests/test_pipeline.py as (type_, pipeline, valid_cases, invalid_cases), with a zero bound on each of ge/gt/le/lt.
applies: pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py constraint application (_apply_constraint) and similar optional-bound handling
